text: Leaning on his elbow, Gabriel looked, without resentment, at her tangled hair and half open mouth, and it hardly pained him now to think how poor a part he, her husband, had played in her life. <break time="0.8s" /> He watched her as though they had never lived together as man and wife, and as he thought of what she must have been in her first girlish beauty, a strange, friendly pity for her entered his soul. <break time="0.8s" /> Soon, he thought, poor Aunt Julia would also become a shade, and it seemed better to pass boldly into that other world in the full glory of some passion than to fade and wither dismally with age. <break time="0.8s" /> Generous tears filled his eyes, for although he had never felt like that himself toward any woman, he knew that such a feeling must be love. <break time="0.8s" /> In the partial darkness he imagined he saw the form of a young man standing under a dripping tree, and his soul approached that region where dwell the vast hosts of the dead. <break time="0.8s" /> His own identity was fading out into a grey, impalpable world, until a few light taps upon the pane made him turn and see the snow, silver and dark, falling obliquely against the lamplight. <break time="0.8s" /> The time had come for him to set out on his journey westward, and snow was general all over Ireland, falling softly upon the Bog of Allen and, further westward, into the dark mutinous Shannon waves. <break time="0.8s" /> It lay thickly drifted on the crooked crosses of the lonely churchyard where Michael Furey lay buried, and his soul swooned slowly as he heard the snow falling faintly through the universe and faintly falling upon all the living and the dead.
